threshold_choice.rule: one additional hidden node id on average (1/164) for design_review_execute.hidden_minus_control and reviewed_change.hidden_paired_gain_mean, with reviewed_change's no-negative-run rule kept
threshold_choice.numeric: written as >= 0.005. With exactly three valued runs per arm (nine designed runs, no replacement), arm means and mean differences are multiples of 1/492: one node on average is 3/492 = 0.0061 and the next lower value is 2/492 = 0.0041, so >= 0.005 admits exactly the results that 1/164 - 1e-12 (the note's tolerance) admits, and floating-point rounding (about 1e-16) cannot cross it. Fixed before any E-B3 run; never adjusted after results

Failed and excluded runs have none. Judge score 0-8 as in E-A and E-B2.

model guard (new since calibration and E-B2): every agent and judge CLI runs with <tree>/.model-guard/claude first on PATH, which refuses a Fable --model or --fallback-model and adds --model claude-opus-5-5 to a claude call without one, and with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1, which pin in-process Claude subagents; the scan reads every Claude session's answering model, and a Fable answer is a hit that cannot be cleared. The shared ~/.claude/settings.json default is claude-fable-5-1, so a nested claude call without a model that calibration's runs would have sent to claude-fable-5-1 now answers with claude-opus-5-5, and any guard bypass reaches claude-fable-5-1. Calibration rung 1 ran without the guard; the guard audit (eb3 evidence cites no-fable-experiments/fable-nested-audit.json) found no Fable session attributed to rung 1's runs or the continuation, within its coverage of session files under the run trees

exclusions: Exactly nine designed runs, records/<arm>/run-1..run-3 under work_root; no run is replaced, relaunched or added. A run is excluded when the controller adjudicates it contaminated (R20; scan hash 1798fc7034d38dc5938472a7cff883b8381703e4) or when it holds a Fable-model hit (scan or the attributed -tmp- sweep; never clearable), every verdict recorded before pool. Infrastructure failures (rate limit, usage limit, auth, CLI crash before agent output; R3) are resumed with resume.sh in the same directory, never relaunched. Every other failure, provider_timeout included, stays a failed run and is never pooled. Any excluded or failed run leaves its arm's claim not evaluated; if budget or quota stops the batch, the affected claims are 'not evaluated'.
fable_halt: A Fable answer found at any time (watchdog tick, scan or sweep) stops new launches and resumes at once; it is recorded and investigated. Launches continue only if the recorded cause lies outside the frozen runtime and needs no runtime change; otherwise the experiment halts without a result. No call that could reach Fable is ever retried.

model_policy: No call in this experiment uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15): arms, nested calls, in-process subagents, judges and every coordination, authoring and review subagent. Allowed Claude answering models: claude-opus-5-5 (planner, Claude judge, guard default, subagent pin) and claude-sonnet-5-5 (reviewed_change coder); OpenAI models gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-sol through Codex. The scan records Fable hits per run and judge. The controller's evidence-only census (eb3/model_census.py, standard library, reusing scan.claude_sessions and scan.answering_model) records answering-model counts per run tree and judge directory, metadata only. Its sweep lists -tmp- project sessions written in the batch window with session id, mtime, cwd and model counts only, and attributes one to a run only when its /tmp/<rel> cwd exists under exactly one E-B3 tree's tmp/ and not on the host /tmp; every other such session is reported unattributed (host sessions default to Fable, so they are expected and only counted). A session started by an absolute CLI path or a reset PATH outside /tmp and outside a tree is invisible to both scan and sweep
hidden_acceptance: summarize.py --python /home/ollie/miniconda3/bin/python (the interpreter that gave the upstream anchor 164/164 and the stub 1/164 in calibration); one summarize over the final pool (all nine runs terminal and adjudicated, both judges terminal, verified and scanned) stands; no patch, hidden fraction or judge score is read before it; any later summarize is reported beside it and never replaces it.
reported: per-run hidden node counts and failing node ids (results.json clones.<id>.hidden_failed), beside the calibration single-call spread (148-154, SD 3.2 node ids)
answering-model counts per run and judge from the census, the sweep's attributed and unattributed counts, and every scan hit with its verdict
verdict_rules: Each claim is judged separately. A claim is 'not evaluated' if any of its <arm>.runs entries is not met or not emitted; otherwise it holds iff all its other entries are met, and a measure summarize does not emit counts as not met. Secondary entries never change a verdict; a gain of exactly 0 is neither positive nor negative. A claim that holds is a directional observation on three runs per arm of one task, not a significance test or a population estimate.
validity: Void unless: mapping.json's task is <runtime>/<task>; the package hash matches at runtime.commit; its judges equal `judges`; every batch carries exactly the `anchors` stems; mapping.json's runtime_commit and every pooled run's record.json runtime_commit equal runtime.commit (checked by the controller); mapping.json's runs are exactly records/<arm>/run-1..run-3 under work_root for the three arms; every pooled run's tree and every counted judge's directory holds .model-guard/claude byte-identical to <runtime>/experiments/compare/shim/model-guard; no pooled run and no counted judge has a Fable-model hit or an attributed Fable sweep session; and the upstream anchor's hidden fraction is 1.0 in every batch, checked before any other measure is read.
anchor_use: Anchor judge scores and hidden fractions are reported; apart from the upstream validity check nothing is adjusted, excluded or re-scored because of them.
judge_rules: Judge scores bear only on secondary entries, but summarize needs at least one judge to emit any measure (a run with no judge score has no value and is not counted in <arm>.runs). A judge is left out only by a contaminated scan verdict or a Fable-model hit recorded, with its reason, before summarize; with one left the report says so; with none, summarize refuses and both claims are not evaluated. A judge stopped by a provider failure is resumed (R38), never re-run.
threshold_provenance: Chosen by the coordinator (threshold_choice) after rung 1's calibration numbers were known and before any E-B3 run. Rung 1's three single calls passed 149, 148 and 154 of 164 (mean 0.917). If the fresh control lands near that level, E-B2's design_review_execute threshold (+0.3) would need a treatment mean above 1.0, so it would be expected to fail unless the fresh control falls far below calibration; the one-node threshold keeps the DRE question answerable at the expected control level. reviewed_change's paired gain compares its final patch with its own first Sonnet patch, whose level is not calibrated, so no headroom is claimed for it; one node on average is used for it for symmetry, with no run negative. One node id is smaller than the calibration single calls' spread (range 6, sample SD 3.2 node ids), so a met claim says the observed means differ in the stated direction by at least one node on this task and these runs; it is not a power calculation, a significance test or an estimate for other tasks. Per-run values are reported beside the calibration spread.
